# 布蘭特突破$100，升息風險與AI支出壓抑債市

## 石油衝擊傳到短端，也傳到科技信用

週四布蘭特升破$100，投資人提高下次聯準會會議升息的機率，美債與科技公司債同步走弱。2年期殖利率上升6個基點至4.37%，10年期升4個基點至4.71%，均接近年內高點。胡塞組織宣稱攻擊紅海的沙烏地油輪，使荷莫茲受阻之外的另一條石油運輸路線也面臨威脅。

10年期跌勢全部來自實質殖利率上升至2.43%，損益兩平通膨率維持2.28%。貨幣市場估計7月升息機率約35%，一週前僅約10%，並已完全計入9月以前升息。初領失業金人數大減至18.7萬，也讓市場更難期待聯準會因需求疲弱而忽略能源風險。

Alphabet提高支出展望，又在主權利率上升之外增加企業融資問題。其債券與甲骨文走弱，微軟、Amazon違約保障變貴；大量潛在發行也遇上2020年4月以來最大單週美國投資級債基金流出。股市同樣下跌，比前幾天更明顯反映金融條件收緊。但融資仍能交易、重整有進展、長天期美債比短端抗跌，調整仍集中在政策預期及資本密集借款人，而非流動性全面消失。

## 失業金數據強勁，市場難以忽略油價

伊朗支持的胡塞組織表示，已攻擊紅海兩艘沙烏地油輪。荷莫茲原已受阻，另一條供應路線再受威脅，增加了燃料與運費長時間偏高的可能。WTI大漲約6.18%至$92.20，布蘭特漲約6.97%至$100.63。

勞動市場沒有提供債券投資人可能期待的抵銷力量。截至7月18日當週，初領失業金減少2.2萬至18.7萬，遠低於中位數預估21萬，數據後殖利率維持強勢。數據明顯低於預期，讓官員更難以就業轉弱為由，暫時忽略能源衝擊。

即使升息25個基點機率約35%，期貨仍以7月28至29日會議維持利率較可能。官員可以選擇等待幾個月核心物價證據，因為升息無法補回受阻的石油供應。不過，等待不等於相信衝擊會很快消退，市場已完全計入9月以前升息。

5年期殖利率升5個基點至4.46%，30年期升2個基點至5.17%。長端升幅較小，使2s10s收窄2個基點至34個基點，2s30s收窄4個基點至80個基點。2年期、5年期、10年期、30年期一週分別升21、18、14、8個基點；一個月升13、17、20、22個基點，仍有累積的長端壓力，但最新賣壓明顯更接近政策期間。

實質殖利率也呈相同順序：5年期升6個基點至2.17%，7年期升5個基點至2.29%，10年期升4個基點至2.43%，20年期升3個基點至2.76%，30年期升2個基點至2.95%。10年期損益兩平通膨率持平，意味著這個年期當天增加的名目殖利率，不是又一輪通膨補償上升。投資人在等待油價是否改變聯準會決策時，要求更高實質報酬。

短券也下跌，包括極短天期。4週券與6週券殖利率各升8、6個基點至3.79%，8週券升14個基點至3.87%；賣壓也延伸至1年期短券。相較本週稍早較平穩的表現，這次連極短天期都明顯走弱。

摩根士丹利對美債中介活動的估計，提供另一個考量。近幾個月投入槓桿基差交易的資本減少逾$2,000億至約$1兆，附買回活動、避險基金期貨空單及資產管理人期貨需求減少，銀行美債庫存則增加，同時套利價差機會變少。這波退場，使約$31兆美債市場在價格失衡時，可吸引進場套利的槓桿資本減少。

較高起始殖利率也提供持有期間緩衝。BlackRock估計，10年期殖利率需再上升約70個基點，一年持有的美債投資才會出現負總報酬，該公司對聯準會的預測也比市場定價溫和。依這項估算，願意承受後續價格波動的投資人，如今可獲得較厚的利息收入緩衝。

## AI支出增加，遇上投資級債基金流出

Alphabet把2026年資本支出預估提高至最多$2,050億，再度引發投資多久才能產生收入、還需要多少債務的疑問。其票息5.5%、2046年到期債券殖利率上升約9個基點至6.11%，較指標殖利率高91個基點。甲骨文2030年到期債殖利率升17個基點至約6.09%，微軟與Amazon違約保障成本也增加。

供需環境也轉趨不利。2026年AI相關借款約達$3,500億，擬議Meta艾爾帕索融資又將增加逾$120億。巴克萊將全年美國投資級發行預測由$1.6兆提高至$1.9兆。同時，截至週三一週，投資人從美國投資級債基金撤出$71億，為2020年4月以來最大。政府殖利率提高總借款成本之際，預期發行量增加，卻遇上基金資金流出。

長天期科技債尤其敏感。Alphabet的£10億、2126年到期債首次跌破90便士，指示價格89.978。其修正存續期間意味著殖利率每升1個百分點，價格可能下跌近15便士。這種現金流遠超過當前投資循環的券，會同時受到主權利率與發行人利差影響。

私人融資仍有分銷管道。Apollo與Blackstone共同安排的$350億Broadcom-Anthropic基礎設施融資，已動用部分約以100至100.5美分流通，其中包括$240億分層中的債權。這是週三收盤後已報交易的後續分銷：透過144A市場，原始私人信貸持有人可將債權轉售給其他合格機構投資人。

新建設貸款條件也受到檢視。Wellington表示，利差已由4年前基準加約4個百分點，壓縮至約2個百分點，部分交易貸款成數卻達90%，本十年稍早約60%。大型雲端業者到2030年預計投入約$5.5兆AI資金，較低貸款利差、較高槓桿，使租戶品質、資產重置價值與技術縮短擔保品使用年限的判斷，容錯空間更小。

交易商正建立整個族群的交易工具。高盛籃子涵蓋18家等權重美國高收益科技發行人，包括CoreWeave、Applied Digital與Cipher Digital，可透過債券或總報酬交換處理$5,000萬至$2.5億詢價。平均殖利率7.45%、利差319個基點，整體高收益市場則為7.3%、267個基點。摩根大通也推出長天期投資級雲端業者與專案發行人籃子。這些工具擴充避險能力，也讓AI成為更明確的信用風險因子。

其他企業方面，Victoria跨過本週稍早仍未達成的同意門檻。HSBC改變立場後，€1.666億、2028年3月到期優先擔保債支持率超過90%，可進行預計減債約£3億的協議式重整。Dish取得法院同意徵求Chapter 11計畫表決，並獲多數Dish DBS債券持有人支持，但基地台業者質疑關係企業債權。Crown Castle表示，依計畫逾$35億損害賠償可能每$1只收回1至2美分。

JetBlue擔保債顯示，有流動性不代表價格不會下修。由會員忠誠計畫擔保的$20億、票息9.875%、2031年到期券，下跌逾2美分至約84，為2024年8月發行後最低。3月底現金及短期投資約$22億，另有未動用$6億循環額度，但燃料與經濟壓力威脅未來現金流，投資人仍在財報前要求更大折價。

葡萄牙計畫先把Azores Airlines約€1.6億債務轉股，再出售至少75%公司。2025年淨損雖縮小近25%至€5,390萬，EBITDA由負轉為€2,150萬，成本下降15%，仍未形成適合出售的資產負債表。債權結果取決於民營化估值與條件，而不只是營運改善方向。

新的結構也把私人資產轉成有評等供給。BlackRock旗下Global Infrastructure Partners討論以逾$10億私人資本持份支持的基金擔保債務，優先部分約基準加250個基點，夾層約475個基點。業界預估2026年CFO發行逾$300億，比2025年增加50%。這讓保險資金更容易接觸私人資產，也與主權及AI債共同爭取承接容量。

Cellnex股價比2021年高點下跌約60%後，正檢視私有化或合併。約€370億企業價值及大量債務，使交易不易。自2022年利率上升後，公司已停止擴張，出售愛爾蘭、奧地利與北歐資產減債。策略性興趣可支持股價，但融資條件才決定交易改善資產負債表，還是增加另一層收購債務。

LQD下跌約0.38%至106.26，HYG與JNK各跌約0.36%至0.37%，分別收79.23、95.40。基金跌幅仍小於部分科技現券的明顯調整，但資金流出與供給預測上修，使承接壓力更加具體。

## ECB維持利率，下一次升息仍在視野內

ECB一致維持存款利率2.25%、再融資利率2.40%、邊際貸款利率2.65%，APP與PEPP繼續到期縮減、不再投資本金。數名官員曾考慮立即緊縮。拉加德形容基礎價格漲幅受控，但強調能源衝擊的強度、期間及潛在第二輪效應，維持逐次會議決策。

市場把結果視為暫停，而非升息結束。10年期德債殖利率一度達3.21%，創2011年以來最高，之後約收3.19%。交換市場幾乎完全計入9月升息25個基點，年底前還接近再一次。6月通膨由3.2%降至2.8%，在布蘭特突破$100後已較難令人放心；天然氣庫存，以及能源如何傳到食品、商品、服務與薪資，對下次決策更重要。

德國國防與基礎設施計畫增加發債，也可能支撐實體需求。市場不只需要承接更多長債，也更難單憑成長轉弱的理由買進。德債殖利率提高，也增加了相對美債的吸引力。

澳洲勞動數據又挑戰了政策轉鬆的期待。6月就業增加7.63萬，超過預估5倍，5月增幅則上修至4.4萬。參與率提高，失業率維持4.4%；澳元一度升0.3%，3年期政府債殖利率最多升5個基點。市場估計9月升息機率約50%，12月以前則完全計入升息25個基點。

日本經濟學家與交易員的看法仍有明顯差距。52名受訪經濟學家中，半數預期下次升息在12月，82%認為大約每半年一次；市場則計入10月以前83%的機率。即使經濟指引重申日本銀行自主性，59%受訪者仍認為高市早苗的政治影響構成限制。日圓疲弱及進口通膨，使定價對每項政策訊號都敏感。

日圓資金也會影響美國槓桿信用。跨幣別交換成本決定日本銀行買進避險後AAA級CLO的收益，進而影響約$1.3兆市場中，管理人能以多低成本發行。農林中央金庫曾占日本銀行CLO投資55%，2019年後監管使持有分散到更在意避險成本的買方。因此，日本政策不一定要先透過美債殖利率，才能影響美國企業融資。

中國則逆全球債市跌勢而行。成長疲弱、股市下跌與貨幣支持預期，推升30年期主權債期貨至11月以來最高，未平倉量一天增加15%至紀錄。存款利率可能調降、政治局可能提供支持的預期，鼓勵投資人買進長債。

但中國同時移除部分弱勢借款人的再融資捷徑。發改委停止讓境內開發商，或以中國境內房產擔保的跨境借款人，使用「1+N」境外貸款。這類工具通常為364天、附展延選項，可在正式外債額度核准前簽訂。要求更早取得核准，減少了時間彈性，即使主權債正因寬鬆預期上漲。

GIC績效反映更長期的配置調整。債券未完全收復跌幅、基金又降低風險，使5年名目年化報酬由6.1%降至3.6%，為2013年以來最低。兩年間美洲配置由44%升至53%，亞太由28%降至22%。這家管理約$9,360億資產的機構，在通膨與債券虧損的長期調整中，也改變了區域配置。

## 南非意外維持利率，匯債付出代價

南非央行出乎市場升息預期，維持政策利率7%。蘭德一度下跌2.5%，報導時跌2.2%至16.76兌$1，10年期政府債殖利率上升16個基點至8.96%。官員在弱成長與燃料通膨間取捨，認為服務價格有問題、商品通膨則較受控。維持利率支撐活動，卻立即付出市場價格代價。

土耳其維持較強的利率防禦，連續第四次維持一週附買回利率37%，有效隔夜貸款利率40%。里拉大致持平於47.23兌$1。6月通膨降至32.1%，為衝突開始後首度放緩，但昂貴石油限制對持續降溫的信心，也延後借款成本下降。

墨西哥整體物價較溫和。7月上半月通膨由6月3.18%降至3.1%，為2020年以來最低，接近3%目標；核心卻小升至3.95%，服務仍為4.36%。央行6月一致維持6.50%，整體數據改善並未解決這些基礎壓力。

肯亞面對債務管理的制度問題。法院認定總統債務審計小組違憲，因為職權屬於審計長。5月底債務占GDP的68.8%，IMF列為高度債務困境風險，新計畫仍在協商。2024年稅案引發抗議後，政府尋求出售國有資產、將未來稅收證券化。裁決未立即改變支付能力，卻提高了後續財政整頓措施合法性的重要性。

主權風險另一端，AAA的盧森堡計畫1月發行€2.5億、3年期零售住宅債；先前€1.5億、3年期國防債支付2.25%，一天售罄。債務低於GDP的30%，向家庭銷售是策略性融資選擇，而不是資金壓力。

EMB下跌約0.59%至94.53，大於美國高收益債基金跌幅。美元更強、美國實質殖利率更高，加上石油上漲，壓縮能源進口經濟體的空間，但各國政策與資產負債表差異仍是關鍵。

## 風險資產開始更明顯反映債市壓力

S&P 500下跌約1.21%至7,408.30，Nasdaq 100跌約1.87%至28,454.81；半導體跌幅較小、約0.54%，但仍比一個月前低約15.65%。VIX上升約12.38%至18.70。Alphabet因支出指引走弱，Tesla因獲利不如預期下跌；大型權值股指標跌4.8%，市值蒸發約$7,970億。

與前幾天不同，殖利率提高已不再伴隨讓人安心的股市反彈。能源與AI支出疑慮一起影響估值，但走勢仍有集中性，而非無差別出清。美元指數上升約0.29%至101.43，把更高美國利率預期傳到外幣融資及進口能源成本。

衝突升級，黃金卻因較高實質殖利率與獲利了結壓過避險需求，下跌約2.29%至$4,051.80。長天期美債仍比短端抗跌，信用債基金跌幅小於EMB。當天環境普遍不利，但損失分布仍反映政策、美元資金與資本密集成長曝險，而不是單一全面撤出資產的浪潮。

## 數據、標售與財報接力，直到聯準會決議

7月24日新屋銷售，7月27日耐久財訂單與2年期、5年期美債標售，以及7月28日7年期標售，接在7月28至29日FOMC之前。活動數據測試高利率對成長的抑制，標售則顯示跌價後買方還要求多少讓步。合併來看，有助判斷目前35%的7月升息機率，是提早反映政策，還是定價過頭。

大型雲端業者財報與融資計畫，則獨立測試信用承接。支出再提高或現金流繼續為負，都會影響新交易商籃子、發行人利差與基金流量。擬議Meta融資是具體發行測試：最終條件及次級表現，將顯示擁擠日程下，合約現金流與更高總殖利率能否吸引買家。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Brent breaks $100 as Fed risk and AI spending weigh on bonds

## The oil shock reaches the front end—and technology credit

Treasuries fell and technology bonds weakened on Thursday as Brent crossed $100 and investors raised the probability of a Fed increase at the coming meeting. The 2-year yield climbed 6 basis points to 4.37%, while the 10-year rose 4 to 4.71%, both near their highest levels of the year. The Houthis' reported attacks on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea threatened another oil route while Hormuz remained disrupted.

The 10-year selloff came entirely through real yields, which rose to 2.43%, while the breakeven held at 2.28%. Money markets put July hike odds around 35%, up from roughly 10% a week earlier, and fully priced an increase by September. Initial jobless claims fell sharply to 187,000, offering little growth-based relief from the renewed concern over energy and policy.

Alphabet's higher spending outlook added a corporate financing problem to the sovereign-rate move. Its bonds and Oracle's weakened, default protection became more expensive for Microsoft and Amazon, and heavy prospective issuance met the largest weekly US high-grade fund outflow since April 2020. Equities also fell, giving more confirmation of tightening conditions than in the preceding sessions. Yet financing continued to trade, restructurings advanced and the long Treasury outperformed the front end: the adjustment remained concentrated in policy expectations and capital-intensive borrowers rather than a general disappearance of liquidity.

## Strong claims data leave little room to look past oil

Iran-backed Houthis said they attacked two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea. With Hormuz already disrupted, the escalation threatened another route for supply and raised the prospect of higher fuel and freight costs lasting longer. WTI surged about 6.18% to $92.20 and Brent about 6.97% to $100.63.

The labor market was not providing the offset that bond investors might have hoped for. Initial claims fell 22,000 to 187,000 in the week ended July 18, well below the 210,000 median estimate, and yields remained firm after the release. The unexpectedly low reading gave officials less reason to look past the energy shock on concerns about weakening employment.

Futures still favored a hold at the July 28–29 Fed meeting, even with about a 35% chance of a quarter-point increase. Officials could choose to wait for several months of core-price evidence because higher rates cannot replace disrupted oil supply. That argument for patience remained distinct from confidence that the shock would fade quickly: an increase was fully priced by September.

The 5-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.46% and the 30-year 2 to 5.17%. The smaller increases at longer maturities narrowed 2s10s 2 basis points to 34 and 2s30s 4 to 80. Over the week, yields were higher by 21, 18, 14 and 8 basis points at two, five, ten and 30 years. Monthly increases of 13, 17, 20 and 22 basis points still showed accumulated long-end pressure, but the latest selling was clearly nearer the policy horizon.

Real yields reinforced that ordering. Five years rose 6 basis points to 2.17%, seven 5 to 2.29%, ten 4 to 2.43%, 20 years 3 to 2.76% and 30 years 2 to 2.95%. The flat 10-year breakeven meant that Thursday's additional nominal yield was not another increase in measured inflation compensation at that maturity. Investors were demanding a higher real return while they waited to see whether the oil shock would change the Fed's decisions.

Bills also cheapened, including short maturities. The 4- and 6-week yields rose 8 and 6 basis points to 3.79%, while the 8-week rose 14 to 3.87%. Selling also extended through one-year bills. The rise at the shortest maturities marked a change from their calmer performance earlier in the week.

Morgan Stanley's assessment of Treasury intermediation added a separate consideration. It estimated that capital committed to leveraged basis trades had declined by more than $200 billion to about $1 trillion in recent months. Lower repo activity, smaller hedge-fund futures shorts, larger bank Treasury inventories and cooler asset-manager futures demand accompanied fewer arbitrage dislocations. The retreat left the roughly $31 trillion market with less leveraged arbitrage capital available to absorb price dislocations.

Higher starting yields also offered a holding-period cushion. BlackRock estimated that the 10-year yield would have to rise roughly another 70 basis points before a one-year Treasury investment produced a negative total return, and judged the priced Fed path more hawkish than its own forecast. The firm's calculation underscored the income cushion now available to investors willing to hold through further price volatility.

## AI spending meets weaker high-grade fund flows

Alphabet raised its projected 2026 capital expenditure to as much as $205 billion, renewing the question of how quickly investment would produce revenue and how much more debt would be needed. Its 5.5% bond due 2046 rose about 9 basis points in yield to 6.11%, or 91 basis points over its benchmark. Oracle's 2030 debt rose 17 basis points in yield to about 6.09%, while Microsoft and Amazon default-protection costs also increased.

The funding backdrop was becoming less comfortable. AI-related borrowing had reached roughly $350 billion during 2026, and the planned Meta-linked El Paso issue would add more than $12 billion. Barclays raised its forecast for annual US high-grade supply to $1.9 trillion from $1.6 trillion. At the same time, investors withdrew $7.1 billion from US high-grade funds in the week through Wednesday, the largest outflow since April 2020. Rising supply expectations were meeting weaker marginal fund demand as government yields lifted all-in borrowing costs.

Long-dated technology bonds were especially exposed. Alphabet's £1 billion issue due 2126 fell below 90 pence for the first time, indicated at 89.978. Its modified duration implied a price decline of almost 15 pence for a one-percentage-point yield increase. Sovereign rates and issuer spreads could therefore reinforce one another in a security whose cash flows extend far beyond the current investment cycle.

Private financing still had distribution channels. Drawn portions of the $35 billion Broadcom-Anthropic infrastructure package, assembled with Apollo and Blackstone, circulated around 100–100.5 cents, including debt from a $24 billion tranche. The ability to distribute to qualified institutional investors through the 144A market widened the buyer base beyond the original private-credit holders, following the initial trading reported after Wednesday's close.

The terms of new construction lending were attracting scrutiny. Wellington said spreads had compressed to about 2 percentage points over benchmarks from roughly 4 four years earlier, while some transactions reached 90% loan-to-value against around 60% earlier in the decade. With hyperscalers expected to spend about $5.5 trillion on AI through 2030, tighter loan margins and higher leverage left less room for error over tenant quality, asset replacement value and how quickly technology could shorten collateral's useful life.

Dealers were creating ways to trade that exposure as a sector. Goldman's basket covered 18 equal-weighted US high-yield technology issuers, including CoreWeave, Applied Digital and Cipher Digital, with $50 million–$250 million inquiries available through bonds or total-return swaps. Average yield was 7.45% and spread 319 basis points, versus 7.3% and 267 for broad high yield. JPMorgan also introduced baskets covering long-dated high-grade hyperscalers and project issuers. The products expanded hedging capacity while making AI a more identifiable credit risk factor.

Elsewhere, Victoria cleared the consent threshold left open earlier in the week. Support exceeded 90% of its €166.6 million March 2028 senior secured notes after HSBC changed position, enabling a consensual transaction intended to cut roughly £300 million of debt. Dish received court approval to solicit Chapter 11 plan votes, with support from holders of most Dish DBS bonds, but tower owners disputed intercompany claims. Crown Castle said more than $3.5 billion of damages could recover only 1–2 cents on the dollar under the plan.

JetBlue's secured bonds showed that liquidity alone did not prevent repricing. Its $2 billion of 9.875% notes due 2031, backed by loyalty-program collateral, fell more than 2 cents to about 84, the lowest since their August 2024 issuance. March-end cash and short-term investments were about $2.2 billion, alongside an undrawn $600 million revolver. Investors still demanded a larger discount ahead of earnings as fuel and economic pressures threatened future cash flow.

Portugal planned to convert about €160 million of Azores Airlines debt to equity before selling at least 75% of the company. The carrier's 2025 loss had narrowed almost 25% to €53.9 million, EBITDA improved to €21.5 million from a deficit and costs fell 15%. Better operations had not yet created a balance sheet ready for sale; creditor outcomes would depend on the privatization's valuation and terms.

New structures were adding rated supply from private assets. BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners discussed a collateralized fund obligation backed by more than $1 billion of private-capital stakes, with senior pricing around 250 basis points over a benchmark and mezzanine near 475. Industry participants expected CFO issuance above $30 billion in 2026, up 50% from 2025. The format broadened insurer access but also competed for capacity alongside sovereign and AI debt.

Cellnex was examining a take-private or merger after its shares fell roughly 60% from their 2021 peak. An enterprise value near €37 billion and substantial debt made a transaction difficult. Since rates began rising in 2022, it had stopped expanding and sold Irish, Austrian and Nordic assets to deleverage. Strategic interest could support the equity, but financing terms would decide whether a deal improved the balance sheet or added acquisition debt.

LQD fell about 0.38% to 106.26, while HYG and JNK each lost about 0.36%–0.37%, closing at 79.23 and 95.40. Fund declines remained modest compared with the sharper adjustments in some cash technology bonds, but outflows and revised supply forecasts made the absorption problem more tangible.

## A European hold still leaves another hike in view

The ECB unanimously held its deposit rate at 2.25%, refinancing rate at 2.40% and marginal lending rate at 2.65%, while continuing APP and PEPP runoff without reinvesting principal. Several officials had considered tightening immediately. Christine Lagarde described underlying price growth as contained but emphasized the energy shock's intensity, duration and potential second-round effects, maintaining a meeting-by-meeting approach.

Markets read the decision as a pause, not the end of tightening. The 10-year Bund reached 3.21%, its highest since 2011, before finishing around 3.19%. Swaps made a quarter-point September increase nearly certain and priced almost another by year-end. June inflation's decline to 2.8% from 3.2% had become less reassuring once Brent exceeded $100. Gas inventories and the spread of energy costs into food, goods, services and wages mattered more for the next decision.

Germany's defense and infrastructure programs added issuance while potentially supporting real demand. That combination increased both the duration offered to investors and the difficulty of finding a straightforward growth-based reason to buy it. Higher Bund yields also gave global portfolios a more competitive alternative to Treasuries.

Australia's labor data supplied another challenge to hopes of easier policy. Employment rose 76,300 in June, more than five times the estimate, after May was revised to a 44,000 gain. Unemployment held at 4.4% as participation increased. The Australian dollar gained as much as 0.3% and the 3-year government yield as much as 5 basis points. Markets assigned around a 50% chance of a September hike and fully priced a quarter-point move by December.

Japan retained a pronounced gap between economists and traders. Half of 52 surveyed economists expected the next BOJ increase in December, and 82% anticipated roughly one move every six months. Markets priced an 83% probability by October. Political influence under Sanae Takaichi was seen as a restraint by 59% of respondents, despite guidelines reaffirming BOJ autonomy. Yen weakness and imported inflation kept pricing sensitive to each policy signal.

Yen funding also affected US leveraged credit. Cross-currency swap costs determine returns for Japanese banks buying hedged AAA CLO tranches, influencing how tightly managers can finance new deals in the roughly $1.3 trillion market. Norinchukin had once held 55% of Japanese banks' CLO investments; regulation after 2019 dispersed ownership toward buyers more responsive to hedging costs. Changes in Japanese policy could therefore reach US corporate funding without moving solely through Treasury yields.

China moved against the global duration selloff. Weak growth, lower stocks and expectations of monetary support lifted 30-year sovereign futures to their highest since November; open interest rose 15% in a day to a record. Speculation about deposit-rate cuts and Politburo support encouraged duration buying.

At the same time, China removed a refinancing shortcut for some weaker borrowers. The NDRC stopped allowing domestic developers, or cross-border borrowers pledging mainland property, to use “1+N” offshore loans—typically 364-day facilities with extension options signed before formal debt-quota approval. Earlier approval requirements reduced timing flexibility, even while sovereign bonds rallied on expectations of easier monetary policy.

GIC's results illustrated the longer portfolio adjustment. Its five-year annualized nominal return fell to 3.6% from 6.1%, the weakest since 2013, as bonds failed to recover fully and the fund reduced risk. Over two years, the Americas allocation rose to 53% from 44%, while Asia-Pacific fell to 22% from 28%. The shift by the roughly $936 billion investor accompanied a prolonged adjustment to inflation and the losses on bonds.

## South Africa's surprise hold brings a currency and bond penalty

The SARB kept its policy rate at 7%, contrary to market expectations of an increase. The rand fell as much as 2.5% and traded 2.2% lower at 16.76 per dollar; the 10-year government yield rose 16 basis points to 8.96%. Policymakers balanced weak growth against fuel-led inflation, describing services pressure as problematic while goods inflation remained more contained. Holding rates supported activity but brought an immediate market cost.

Turkey maintained a tighter defense. It held the one-week repo rate at 37% for a fourth meeting and effective overnight lending at 40%. The lira was little changed near 47.23 per dollar. June inflation eased to 32.1%, the first slowdown since the conflict began, but expensive oil limited confidence in sustained disinflation and delayed borrowing-cost relief.

Mexico's headline picture was milder. Inflation slowed to 3.1% in the first half of July from 3.18% in June, the lowest since 2020 and close to the 3% target. Core inflation edged up to 3.95%, however, and services remained at 4.36%. Banxico had unanimously held at 6.50% in June; the headline improvement did not resolve those underlying pressures.

Kenya faced an institutional debt-management question. A court ruled a presidential debt-audit panel unconstitutional because the mandate belonged to the auditor-general. Debt stood at 68.8% of GDP at end-May, the IMF classified the country at high risk of debt distress and talks on a new program continued. Following protests against the 2024 tax plan, the government had pursued state-asset sales and securitization of future tax receipts. The ruling left payment capacity unchanged immediately but raised the importance of legal legitimacy for the next consolidation measures.

At the opposite end of the sovereign spectrum, AAA-rated Luxembourg planned a €250 million three-year retail housing bond in January. A €150 million three-year defense bond paying 2.25% had sold out in one day. With debt below 30% of GDP, household distribution was a strategic funding choice rather than evidence of pressure. 

EMB fell about 0.59% to 94.53, more than the US high-yield fund declines, as a stronger dollar, higher US real yields and oil narrowed the room for importing economies. Country policy and balance-sheet differences nevertheless remained decisive.

## Risk assets now reflect more of the bond-market pressure

The S&P 500 fell about 1.21% to 7,408.30 and the Nasdaq 100 about 1.87% to 28,454.81. Semiconductors lost a smaller 0.54% but remained about 15.65% below a month earlier. VIX rose about 12.38% to 18.70. Alphabet weakened on spending guidance and Tesla on a profit disappointment; a broad megacap gauge fell 4.8%, erasing roughly $797 billion of value.

Unlike the preceding sessions, higher yields were no longer coexisting with a reassuring equity rebound. Energy and AI spending concerns were reaching valuations together, although the moves remained concentrated rather than indiscriminate. The dollar index gained about 0.29% to 101.43, transmitting higher US rate expectations into foreign-currency funding and imported-energy costs.

Gold fell about 2.29% to $4,051.80 despite escalating conflict as higher real yields and profit-taking outweighed haven demand. Long Treasuries still outperformed the front end and credit funds lost less than EMB. The session was broadly adverse, but the distribution of losses continued to reflect exposure to policy, dollar funding and capital-intensive growth rather than a single rush out of all assets.

## Data, auctions and earnings lead into the Fed decision

New-home sales on July 24, durable-goods orders and the 2- and 5-year Treasury auctions on July 27, then the 7-year sale on July 28, precede the July 28–29 FOMC. Activity releases will test the growth restraint from high rates, while auctions show how much concession buyers require after the selloff. Together they will help assess whether the current 35% July hike probability is an early policy signal or an overshoot.

Hyperscaler earnings and financing plans will test credit capacity separately. Further spending increases or negative cash flow would add pressure to the new dealer baskets, issuer spreads and fund flows. The planned Meta-linked financing provides a concrete placement test: final terms and secondary performance will show whether contracted cash flow and higher all-in yields can draw buyers despite the crowded pipeline.

The MAS decision on July 27 and BOJ meeting at month-end add imported-inflation tests. Singapore's core inflation near 1.6% offers room for patience, but a 17% electricity-tariff increase could change the assessment. Japan's guidance will test the gap between the economists' December consensus and more aggressive market pricing. The yen, JGB front end and domestic duration demand will show how that decision affects the relative appeal of foreign bonds.
